manualSetup.text: Android: install a JDK 17 or 21 and set JAVA_HOME; install Android Studio with the SDK platform-tools and an emulator image, set ANDROID_HOME and add <sdk>/platform-tools to PATH. Start an emulator (or connect a phone with USB debugging on); `adb devices` must list it.

iOS: needs a Mac with Xcode (one of the latest two versions). Run `xcode-select --install`, open Xcode once to accept the licence, and boot a simulator (`xcrun simctl list devices`). Put its name and version in DEVICE_NAME and PLATFORM_VERSION. Simulators need a simulator build (.app); real devices need a signed .ipa. Without a Mac, run on BrowserStack instead.
Windows: Windows 10 or 11. Appium, the driver and the app run on the same Windows machine. Set APP_PATH to the installed .exe (or APP_ID to a Store app's AUMID).
macOS: macOS 11.3+ with Xcode 13+. Give Xcode Helper Accessibility permission (System Settings → Privacy & Security → Accessibility). Set APP_ID to the app's bundle id, or APP_PATH to the .app.

Check the driver with `npx appium driver doctor <driver>` (uiautomator2, xcuitest, mac2, …), then start Appium with `npm run appium` and leave it running while tests run (it listens on APPIUM_SERVER_URL, default http://127.0.0.1:4723).
Put the app build in the git-ignored apps/ folder and set APP_PATH (TestPilot fills it in when you answer the app step), or set APP_ID to run an app already installed on the device.

BrowserStack: upload the build with `curl -u "$BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME:$BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY" -X POST https://api-cloud.browserstack.com/app-automate/upload -F file=@apps/<your-build>` and put the returned bs:// id in BROWSERSTACK_APP_ID (uploads expire after 30 days). Then run `npm run test:browserstack`. BrowserStack supports WebdriverIO up to 9 and Appium up to 3.5.2, so keep these versions pinned.
